chapter: Blue Devils, Moten and the Reno Club
title: Moten's band and its records
summary: Basie says Moten's band was well known outside Kansas City because it made records and sold them well.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: "Back in the early '30s, there was a band in Kansas City that more or less ruled the local jazz scene. It was that of the late Benny Moten."

"Pew people outside of Kansas City ever knew much about this band for the reason that way back then, there were no such means of nationwide exploitation as radio, records and jukeboxes and local or territorial bands had to be seen to be heard." Did you say that?
Uh-huh. That's the way he saw it. But Benny had records. (Inaudible). He was pretty well known for his records.
Benny was a pretty good record seller.
So that he was known outside of K.C.?
Well, "the Blue Devils broke up and several of us, including Page and Rushing, --" Would you have called --
Would you have said Page? Do you
We were calling him everything. We called him Page (inaudible).
Talking about it, would you call him Page?
I probably would. I probably would have said Page.
I probably would have said Page.
I'd say Jimmy. I might have said -- maybe I, you know --
